overview: After 1.b3 d5 White plays 2.Ba3, aiming to trade the dark-squared bishops and stop Black castling comfortably. Black develops with ...Nf6 and ...e6 or ...c5, accepting the exchange on f8. The play is quiet and the line is a rare try.

white_ideas.idea: Trade bishops or pressure the dark squares from a3
Develop with e3, Nf3 and c4

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre while White bishop stands on a3

typical_structures.structure: Black central pawns versus White flank play

character.notes: After 2.Ba3 White offers to trade the dark-squared bishops and play slowly; no forcing lines.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: Playable but gains little; Black castles after ...e6 and ...c5 without trouble.

structure.notes: Flank opening where neither side has committed the centre pawns beyond ...d5.

approach.notes: Strong players use 2.Bb2 instead; the Graz move is a rare surprise.

level.notes: Little theory and no deep plan.
